title: W1 fix is partial: the two em-dash strings were rewritten, but the claimed `no_em_dash_test` extension to scan refcheck copy never landed — the RT CI ban still doesn't reach the panel's copy
evidence: client/test/copy_test.gleam:308-316 — `no_em_dash_test` iterates only `for_each_copy` (all_codes() x all_contexts(), i.e. toast/page copy); `grep -c refcheck client/test/copy_test.gleam` = 0 and no em-dash scan over refcheck strings exists anywhere in client/test. The r1 fix map claims 'no_em_dash_test extended to scan refcheck consts'; it was not. The strings themselves are fixed (copy.gleam:665 'Unmoderated referee text: written by the referee, not reviewed by us.' and :825 'Applicant nudge: couldn't send' — both em-dash-free, verified; all remaining em-dashes in refcheck copy are spec-verbatim from §7.4/§7.5/§7.8/§10.3, verified against ux-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md).
detail: Round-2 mandate: a missing half of a claimed fix is itself a finding at the r1 severity. The primary defect (shipped em-dashes) is gone, but the CI pin that was part of the claimed fix is absent: the ban test still cannot see the refcheck consts, so a future implementer-authored panel string with an em-dash would again ship with CI green — the exact gap r1 called out ('the ban test doesn't reach refcheck consts, so CI stays green'). Note the extension cannot be a blanket scan of all refcheck consts (spec-verbatim strings legitimately carry em-dashes), so it needs an explicit allowlist/denylist — which is presumably why it was skipped, but the fix map claim remains unmet and no alternative pin exists.
recommended_fix: Add a test that scans the implementer-authored refcheck strings (or all refcheck consts minus an explicit spec-verbatim allowlist) for U+2014, or amend the r1 fix record to document why the pin was dropped.

title: reference_panel.gleam GREW in the rework (1263 -> 1309 lines) — the r1 module-split recommendation was not taken and the module remains ~3.3x the <400 view-module target
evidence: git diff 9d66ce9 e0f9fa7 --stat: reference_panel.gleam +190/-119 net growth; wc -l = 1309 vs r1's 1263. The module still bundles view code, the parsed-result JSON decoders (signals/form_session/ai_summary), word/object renderers, and worth-knowing threshold logic in one file.
detail: Per the architecture lens brief: note-level either way, but flag if it GREW. The rework added the relationship_other insertion, chronological timeline sort, count-set split, answered-count rewrite, and doc comments inline rather than extracting the result-parsing half into a sibling module (e.g. reference_panel_result.gleam) as r1 recommended. Guideline-level only; no behaviour impact.
recommended_fix: Move the result-parsing/render half (decoders, render_value family, worth_knowing_signals) into a sibling module when RC4.3 touches this file.

title: N2 fix is partial: `normalize_datetime` swaps the space separator but the Postgres ::text colon-less offset ('+00') remains — the Form-opened line's <time datetime> is still not a valid HTML datetime value
evidence: Integration wire pin asserts "form_opened_at":"2026-08-01 21:12:00+00" (server/test/integration/reference_detail_payload_integration_test.gleam:307). normalize_datetime (reference_panel.gleam:597-601) is `string.replace(at, " ", "T")`, yielding "2026-08-01T21:12:00+00" for the datetime attribute. Per the WHATWG HTML spec a valid time-zone offset string is 'Z' or a sign + two-digit hour + ':' + two-digit minute — '+00' without minutes is not valid, exactly the 'colon-less offset' r1 N2 named as the invalid part.
detail: The r1 note's complaint ('colon-less offset is not a valid HTML datetime value') is only half-addressed: the space->T separator swap landed (r1 fix map 'datetime normalization'), but the resulting value is still machine-unparseable as HTML datetime, so screen readers/browsers that parse the attribute still cannot resolve the Form-opened timestamp. The visible text is formatted correctly via format_timestamp_short, so impact is limited to the attribute's machine readability. Attempt-log entries are unaffected (RFC3339 'Z' values pass through).
recommended_fix: Extend normalize_datetime (or the SQL to_char) to emit RFC3339: append ':00' to a trailing bare +hh/-hh offset, or map the UTC offset to 'Z'.
